question: Shuttle engines burned 6 kg of oxygen (1,141 kg/m³) per kg of hydrogen (71 kg/m³). How many times more tank volume did hydrogen need?
move: Weigh and measure separately; the lightest ingredient can fill the room.
trap: Assuming the ingredient used in the smaller amount needs the smaller tank.
hint: Find how many times denser the oxygen is, then allow for its six-fold mass.
steps: 1 kg of hydrogen fills 1 ÷ 71 ≈ 0.0141 m³, about 14.1 litres.
6 kg of oxygen fill 6 ÷ 1,141 ≈ 0.0053 m³, about 5.3 litres.
source: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 2004
reference: Lide (ed.), CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 85th ed., CRC Press, 2004
